Shein to open first permanent UK store in Manchester

Published 2026-10-06 10:00 UTC

Online fast fashion giant Shein is opening its first permanent shop in the UK, in Manchester's Arndale shopping centre, next month. The company has previously run temporary pop-up stores in London and Birmingham.

Shein, founded in China and now headquartered in Singapore, sells most of its clothes through its app. The retailer has faced criticism over working conditions in its supply chain and the environmental impact of fast fashion, which it says it is addressing.

The 1,200 square metre store will employ about 60 people. Retail analysts said the move showed online-first brands were looking to physical shops to reach new customers and cut the cost of returns.

The store will occupy two floors of a shopping centre in Manchester city centre and is expected to employ around 150 people. It will stock clothing, accessories and homeware, and customers will be able to collect and return online orders there.

Shein, founded in China and now headquartered in Singapore, has built its business on very low prices and a constant stream of new designs sold online. It has opened temporary pop-up shops in the UK before, but this is its first permanent physical store in the country.

The company has faced criticism over working conditions in its supply chain and the environmental impact of fast fashion. Campaigners said a permanent store would encourage more consumption of cheap clothing that is quickly thrown away. Shein says it has improved supplier audits and launched a resale platform for used items.

Retail analysts said the move shows how online retailers are increasingly using physical shops to build brand awareness and reduce the cost of returns. Shein is also preparing a possible stock market listing, and a stronger presence on the high street could help it appeal to investors.

Manchester's council welcomed the jobs, saying the store would help bring shoppers back to the city centre. Rival fashion retailers are expected to respond with more aggressive pricing ahead of Christmas.
